data.arc: Mid‑2025 the market was dominated by AI mega‑funding, highlighted by Thinking Machines Lab’s $2 billion Series A and a $300 million secondary sale from XAI, while African capital grew 40 % YoY but remained concentrated. July amplified the AI surge with a $2 billion raise at a $12 billion valuation and expanding MENA activity, but August saw a 25 % YoY decline in global funding and a 44 % plunge in seed‑stage capital, underscoring a more selective climate and governance scrutiny. September revived confidence with large late‑stage raises such as Commonwealth Fusion’s $863 million and emerging‑market fintech inflows, and October introduced regional swings as Asia surged, Africa slipped, and Wayve pursued a $2 billion round amid warnings of AI‑washing. November highlighted a mixed but robust landscape with Japan’s AI firms securing over ¥35 billion, Africa’s funding jumping 215.7 % YoY, and India’s private funding slipping 32 % while AI firms like Cursor and Harmonic raised significant capital. The new year began with a rebound in AI funding ($500 million in 2025), highly concentrated African capital (>92 % captured by the top 10), and rising gender diversity in India (>45 % of startups with a woman director or founder), setting the stage for continued mega‑AI rounds such as Anthropic’s $65 billion financing in May.

turning_points.why: AI mega‑funding surged with a $2 billion raise at a $12 billion valuation and MENA investment expanded, indicating heightened investor appetite.
Global funding fell 25 % YoY and seed‑stage capital plunged 44 %, marking a shift toward selectivity and heightened governance scrutiny.
Regional funding swings emerged as Asia surged, Africa slipped, and Wayve pursued a $2 billion round amid warnings of AI‑washing, highlighting market polarization.

AI funding rebounded with nearly $500 million raised in 2025, African capital became highly concentrated (>92 % with top 10), and women’s participation rose above 45 %, signaling new investment focus.
Anthropic secured a historic $65 billion financing round, pushing its valuation toward $1 trillion and reshaping the AI funding landscape.
